name: The Ritz-Carlton Georgetown
positioning: Redbrick Ritz-Carlton hotel with a smokestack, in a former 1932 industrial building on the Potomac in Georgetown (official name: The Ritz-Carlton Georgetown, Washington, D.C.)
best_for: Travelers who want a historic, residential-style base in Georgetown
Guests who like suites with fireplaces, terraces and dining spaces

facts.text: The hotel occupies a turn-of-the-century industrial building built in 1932.
The hotel was built on the site of an incinerator and is a National Historic Landmark.
The hotel is in the heart of Georgetown, just steps from M Street and Wisconsin Avenue.
The hotel overlooks the Potomac River and is near Georgetown University and the C&O Canal.
Rooms overlook the neighborhood or the Potomac River, and suites feature patios, dining spaces and fireplaces.
The Ambassador Suite is inspired by Georgetown row houses and has a personal study off the main living room.
Degrees Bistro serves contemporary American dishes among brick walls and steel beams, with the wine bar in the center of the room.
The spa has five treatment rooms, including one couple's room, and uses an ESPA product line.
The spa has relaxation lounges with saunas and steam rooms.
The fitness center has Technogym equipment, Peloton spin bikes and a wall bar by PENT.
The hotel lends Ritz-Carlton Cruisers, city-friendly bikes for getting to attractions such as the National Mall and the Smithsonian Museums.

highlights.text: The redbrick hotel has a smokestack and mixes the Potomac's industrial history with a sleek, modern design.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite has a private terrace with lounge seating and a private fire-pit.
The Living Room has exposed brick, a wood-burning fireplace and lounge seating.
Baked Alaska is served every evening in The Living Room.
Children are welcomed with a red wagon of stuffed animals they can take home as a souvenir.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have an airport shuttle.
WhataHotel notes limited parking availability in the Georgetown area.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing typical of Ritz-Carlton properties.
